💼 Past Experience & Track Record
For President - Batch 2024 & General Secretary of Academic Affairs
I currently work as a High Performance Computing Research Intern at the University of Maryland, where I engineered a hybrid numerical framework that delivered a 2200x runtime speedup on a lattice QCD research project, and built a production-grade analysis pipeline (Python/C++, HDF5, parallelized computation) that cut processing time from nearly 2000 seconds to 97. I'm also a Research Affiliate in Algorithmic Fairness at UC Berkeley, studying bias propagation in ranking algorithms. Separately, I built and led Study with Gremlin, an adaptive productivity platform, from idea to shipped product, and was competitively selected for the MIT-affiliated LaunchX Entrepreneurship Program. I completed a remote international semester at Hanyang University, Seoul, and maintain a strong CS Core GPA alongside coursework in Operating Systems, Computer Architecture, and Optimization Techniques. Alongside all of this, I've personally guided 7-10 peers and juniors at JKLU on research opportunities, internships, and academic pathways, helping them figure out labs to target, how to reach out, and how to structure strong applications.
🎯 Why Should We Choose You?
For President - Batch 2024 & General Secretary of Academic Affairs
Academic Affairs on paper is easy a functioning one is hard, because it requires follow-through, not just good intentions. That's what I bring. My work across research labs and building my own product from scratch has taught me how to take a vague goal and turn it into a structured, running system with actual accountability. I want to bring that same discipline to three concrete things: Structured, recurring GATE/CAT peer-prep groups, run on a fixed cadence, not ad hoc, drawing on how I've organized my own research and prep workflows. A real feedback loop with OAA, short check-ins each semester, not a suggestion box, so grievances and resource gaps (library access, digital resources) get tracked with MoMs that actually lead to follow-up. More accessible faculty-student touchpoints, modeled on the mentor relationships I've built at Maryland and Berkeley, so students see faculty interaction as approachable rather than intimidating. I'm not proposing this from the outside. I've already spent my time here doing an informal version of this role, guiding 7-10 peers on research opportunities and academic pathways one-on-one, without any title attached. This position would let me take that same instinct and make it structured and scalable for the wider student body, instead of just word-of-mouth.

💼 Past Experience & Track Record
For Club Co-Chair - Batch 2026 & Mess Coordinator
I have worked with team of local MLA for the vaccination drive of my area of dogs. I gained a great experience from that I have been always fond of volunteering. I have always been found of helping people and animals, I strongly feel empathetic towards them and would love to continue with this.
🎯 Why Should We Choose You?
For Club Co-Chair - Batch 2026 & Mess Coordinator
During a dog vaccination drive with a local MLA's team, I saw how much difference a small, organized effort can make for a community's most voiceless members, people who can't speak up for themselves, and animals who obviously can't either. That's why I want this role: not to add a line to my resume, but because I want to keep showing up, organizing drives, working with NGOs, finding the small ways we can help the people and animals around us. As Co-Chair, I'd want the club to think of "community" a little more broadly than it usually does. When we talk about community development, we mostly mean people, and that matters, obviously but animals are part of this community too, and they need us just as much. I'd want us to make space for that. And just as importantly, I want to make it easy for other students to find their own way into causes that matter, so this isn't something one person carries it becomes something the club just keeps doing.
Coordinator Preferred Post #2: Mess Coordinator
💼 Past Experience & Track Record
For Mess Coordinator
I have been in hostel for 2 years prior than this in Birla Public School (A school of bits) I know how mess works and what needs work upon, I have also been a mess leader for my house, so I know exactly what changes to bring and what can't be done
🎯 Why Should We Choose You?
For Mess Coordinator
I've spent two years in a hostel, at Birla Public School, Pilani, before this, so I've basically lived through the mess system, not just eaten in it. When you're there that long, you start noticing things. What actually bothers people versus what they just complain about once and move on from. What issues keep coming back no matter what anyone tries. And where mess committees usually overpromise and then don't really deliver. I don't have some official title to back this up, but I think that's fine, maybe even better. I've seen this purely as a student, which is kind of the point, right? That's the perspective that actually matters. So I'd rather bring a couple of changes that are realistic and actually doable, instead of a long list that sounds nice but falls apart the second you try to run it.
